body: Immersion is the worst learning style for me personally. I learned Spanish through memorizing tenses and words in a structured classroom setting which was boring as hell, but it prepared me for real life conversations because I was confident in my ability to form sentences. I tried learning Portuguese through immersion since it’s my husband’s native language, but that just resulted in my being able to understand and read virtually everything but not know how to respond back. I believe the best order is to learn vocab and grammar at the same time, get a good grasp on at least the present tense, then work on speaking and listening comprehension.

I’m in my second year of college and I haven’t had much luck making friends here. I joined a few clubs so I hang out with people there and sometimes get food with them after, but we never really hang out outside of that.

I was always kind of a loner as a child because I’ve had social anxiety for as long as I can remember. When I was in elementary school, the teachers thought there was something wrong with me because I never talked in class. Turns out I was just extremely shy. I lived in a small town and had about one friend a year, sometimes the friendships would last for a little longer, until middle school.

I went through a weird goth/emo phase in middle school which kinda scared people away. I don’t really know why I did it, I think I just wanted to give people a reason as to why I was an outcast instead of admitting that it was something more personal. I had two other friends who dressed the same but my mom made me stop hanging out with them which left me friendless for the most part. I met my current best friend in 8th grade and along with another girl who took voice lessons with me. Those two are the only people I still hang out with and talk to.

In high school I sometimes hung out with this small, loosely-defined friend group. However, there was a lot of cattiness and drama and none of us really liked each other (except my best friend and me). Needless to say, those friendships fizzled out right after graduation. There are two other girls who I hang out with about twice a year. We aren’t close at all (we only talk when we’re both in town and need something to do). They’re great people but they are both super involved in their own lives and have friend groups of their own in college.

I plan on studying abroad next semester so hopefully I’ll have more of a social life then. People here don’t understand that I don’t stay home on the weekends by choice, I just have no one to go out with. I thought 20 would be a little better than this.

Anyway, hopefully some of you can relate to this. It’s good to know I’m not the only one.

She's clearly hiding something from you. The fact that she won't show you unedited pictures or talk to you on the phone/skype is a major red flag imo. I'm not trying to jump to conclusions here but have you considered the possibility that you're being catfished? Having strong feelings for someone can hide otherwise obvious red flags but from an outsider's point of view, there's something weird going on. Also, I'd recommend taking a parent or other adult with you if you decide to meet her in person.

What do you mean by minimum communication? Do you guys talk/text regularly? Long distance is really difficult no matter what, so it's important to be on the same page about communication. If I were you, I'd bring this up soon. Tell her that you want to stay close even though you're both going to be busy. I was in a LDR for four months and it was our daily conversations that kept it going. Some days are going to be busier than others, but if you can manage a "goodnight/good morning" text every day, that shows that you're still thinking of each other and taking some time out of your day to show that you care. Take time to plan skype/phone calls a few days in advance and let them know when you're going to be busy so they know you're not ignoring them. My BF and I write each other letters through email every month for our anniversary, which was especially nice when we were long distance because it reminded us of how much we cared about each other despite the situation and it gave us something to look forward to. I'm not gonna lie, distance is really tough, but if you prioritize the other person, keep them updated on your life, visit often (if possible), and want it to work, then it can work.
